Authorize your one registered geometry readback using the 51 saved S4R_measure_496000 records, within 15 minutes of executable diagnostic time. Keep its older code/lesson-route scope explicit. Compare forecasts and measured poses with identical frames, origins and composition. Report geometric residuals and measured-reference error; this cannot validate the launched planner or shoulder/wrist limits. Do not manufacture those missing results or rerun training to fill them."
scope: lesson-route tenure forecasts of executed commands on code d6a12e317, grouped by the author the observer's model lane records at each command's start step: planner (the intention output; here the sensory goal search, --planner-search trust_v2 with --physical-goals off; babble skipped), reflex_noise (the motor controller's command plus babble) and reflex (the motor controller's command without noise). They cannot validate the launched planner, shoulder or wrist limits. eff_exp_cm and eff_exp_deg are the body head's tenure output (lem/model/efference.py EfferenceHeads.body, columns 6 to 11, times 1.80 cm and 11.0 degrees) formed in the training lesson where each executed command began, from the delayed next-frame lesson's latent (the learning route), for the command the body executed. Run S4R_measure_496000 holds no pose-return search, no iteration-0 composite and no selected-command pose forecast. Its code (d6a12e317) precedes the canonical quaternion sign of the head's command input: canonical_order_quaternions entered at commit 5b55b57f7 and BODY_INPUT_VERSION (canonical_quaternion_sign_v1) at 7870777f0, both descendants of d6a12e317; the launched pose-return code (f0183150b) holds both. The readings measure the composition rule forecast_pose uses (each handle's start pose plus its own change) on these forecasts; they say nothing about the launched planner's forecasts or about the shoulder or wrist joint limits.
what_is_compared: S = the measured pose at model step eff_began (trajectory bones of that body and model step: x y z w world quaternion, world cm); E = the measured pose at eff_began + 5 (the command's tenure, --motor-hold 5); F = the forecast: S composed with eff_exp_cm and eff_exp_deg by forecast_pose's rule (position = S + change in cm; orientation = rotvec_to_quat(change in degrees x pi / 180) x S, x y z w, the formulas of lem/model/motor_synergy.py quat_mul and rotvec_to_quat); C = the control: S composed with the measured change eff_ach_cm and eff_ach_deg by the same rule; the identity conditions check that C reproduces E within the bounds the storage allows (identity), and C is the noise floor F is read against. Every handle is its MuJoCo body origin (mimo_bridge/proprio_adapter.py: xpos x 100 and xquat); every orientation of a body handle is a world x y z w quaternion (the gaze row is head-relative, conj(head) x eye in proprio_adapter.read, and is not used); a link residual is expressed in the parent handle's frame of the same pose. Nothing is projected, fitted or clamped: F is read as composed (quaternions are divided by their length before they turn a vector; quaternion_norm_deviation gives how far from 1 that length was).
not_tested: the launched pose-return search's forecasts (selected command and iteration-0 composite): no file holds them per handle; this check does not stand in for them
shoulder joint limits (three hinges at the upper-arm origin; not decomposed into angles)
wrist joint limits (three hinges anchored off the hand origin; not decomposed into angles)
contacts other than the floor plane (self-contact, the crib, objects); the floor readings use body origins only
the trunk below the chest (lower_trunk and the bodies between it and the chest)
the finger, head, leg, foot and gaze handles: the readings cover the chest, upper arms, lower arms and wrists; the position and turn identity conditions cover all 25 non-gaze handles
verdict_rule: a reading check, not a feasibility test: pass when every condition holds (51 tenure records with 8 bodies read; every record-body entry joined to measured start and end poses or listed because its start or end model step lies outside the trajectory's recorded steps or the episode changed between them; C reproduces E within the storage bounds; every recorded pose meets the scene XML's links and elbow hinge within float32 rounding; every input matches its MANIFEST.json entry; the scope reads as stated; the reference geometry read; every declared reading computed and finite; finished inside the 300 s bound); fail otherwise. The readings measure link residuals (cm), the elbow's off-axis turn and its angle beyond two ranges (degrees), the forearm-to-hand distance beyond its recorded range (cm) and origin heights below two lines (cm). Feasibility is not judged: no new scoring rule is formed, and shoulder and wrist limits and contacts other than the floor plane are not tested.

measured_reference_geometry.definition: the same readings on every recorded pose of the trajectory (all bodies, all model steps): the reference's own error against the scene XML (bounded by the links and elbow identity conditions), and the recorded ranges and lowest heights the forecasts are read against

readings_definitions.shoulder_link: |R(chest)^-1 (p_upperarm - p_chest) - o_shoulder| cm; o_shoulder = the upper arm's body pos in the chest frame (scene XML); its three hinges sit at the upper-arm origin
readings_definitions.upperarm_link: |R(upperarm)^-1 (p_lowerarm - p_upperarm) - o_elbow| cm; o_elbow = the lower arm's body pos in the upper-arm frame; the elbow hinge sits at the lower-arm origin
readings_definitions.elbow_off_axis_turn: the rotation vector (degrees) of R(upperarm)^-1 R(lowerarm) minus its component along the elbow axis: its length (a hinge reads 0)
readings_definitions.elbow_beyond_scene_range: degrees of the on-axis component beyond the scene XML's elbow range (0 inside)
readings_definitions.elbow_beyond_recorded_range: the same beyond the range read on the trajectory's recorded poses
readings_definitions.forearm_to_hand_outside_recorded_range: |p_wrist - p_lowerarm| cm beyond the range read on the recorded poses (not a rigid link: the wrist hinges sit off the hand origin)
readings_definitions.below_floor_plane: max(0, floor plane z - origin z) cm. BODY ORIGINS ONLY: each segment's geoms reach past its origin (the upper-arm and forearm capsule radii, 2.50 and 2.40 cm in this scene, are listed under reference_geometry), so 0 does not mean the arm stayed above the floor
readings_definitions.below_lowest_measured_height: max(0, the handle's lowest recorded z - origin z) cm; body origins only, as above
readings_definitions.each_reading: n, min, median, 90th percentile (linear interpolation) and max of F, C, S and E; C's maximum; the count of F above C's maximum; F divided by the child handle's forecast movement (|eff_exp_cm| of the child for cm readings, |eff_exp_deg| of the lower arm for the elbow; 0 = link kept, 1 = a residual as large as the forecast movement)

measured_reference_error.definition: C against E per pair and handle: |C position - E position| (cm) and the turn between C's and E's orientations (degrees). C composes the stored float16 measured change exactly as F composes the forecast change, so this is the error of the composition path and its storage (bounded by the position and turn identity conditions): the noise floor F's residuals are read against

forecast_vs_measured_end.definition: F against E per pair and handle: |F position - E position| (cm), the turn between F's and E's orientations (degrees), beside how far the forecast moved the handle and how far it really moved (cm) and how far the forecast turned it (degrees)

definition.u: 2^-24, the float32 unit roundoff; u64 = 2^-53, the float64 unit roundoff
definition.position: per joined pair, body handle (the 25 non-gaze rows) and axis: |C - E| <= h16 + u(1+u)^2 (|S| + |E|) + (2u + u^2)|E - S| + 2 u64 (|C| + |E|) cm. h16 = half the float16 spacing at the stored change (np.spacing of the stored value / 2: the lane's float16 rounding); the lesson formed the change in float32 as ((E / 200) - (S / 200)) x 200 from float32 poses (mimo_bridge/datasource.py divides the world cm by 200; lem/model/efference.py pose_change): each division rounds by u relative, the subtraction and the product by u each; the last term is this program's float64 sum and difference
definition.turn: per joined pair and body handle: the turn between C and E <= the length of the three per-axis float16 half spacings of the stored turn + ((8 pi + 3) u rad + 10 u |stored turn|) in degrees + 64 u64 x 180 degrees. The lesson formed the turn in float32 from the same float32 quaternions (efference.rotation_change_deg): each relative-quaternion component is a 4-term dot product of unit quaternions (error <= 4u, Higham's gamma_4), so the quaternion moves by <= 8u and the rotation by <= 16u rad; a rotation vector moves by at most pi/2 times the rotation change for turns up to 180 degrees: 8 pi u rad; the norm, atan2 (up to 3 ulp), division, product and degree conversion add <= 3u rad and 10u relative; the exponential map moves an orientation by at most the rotation-vector change (Lipschitz 1); the last term is this program's float64
definition.links: on every recorded pose, the shoulder and upper-arm link residuals <= u (|p_child| + |p_parent|) + 2u(1+2u)|p_child - p_parent| + 64 u64 (|p_child| + |p_parent| + |p_child - p_parent|) cm: the trajectory holds float32 roundings of MuJoCo's float64 xpos x 100 (<= u|p| per axis) and xquat (<= u per component, so each normalized orientation is off by <= 2u(1+2u) rad), and MuJoCo places a child origin at the parent origin plus the parent rotation times the XML pos when the child's hinges sit at its origin
definition.elbow: on every recorded pose, the elbow's off-axis turn <= 360 u (1+2u) + 64 u64 x 180 degrees: the two orientations are off by <= 4u(1+2u) rad together and a rotation vector moves by at most pi/2 times that
definition.float64_terms: the 64 u64 terms count MuJoCo's and this program's float64 rounding as at most 64 steps of 2^-53
definition.breaks_on: a trajectory of another attempt, a scene XML of another body age or a join one model step off exceed these bounds
